producer_report.summary: Added `check_job_size` to the reading gate. Root cause: nothing before dispatch measured whether a request fits one producer run, so jobs 20261025-183644-t67q and 20261017-205554-zaj2 passed every reading check, were dispatched, and ended with no change. The check is a `step!` in `refusing_check`, placed second after `check_prior_result_and_scope`. It maps each deliverable other than CHANGELOG.md to a group: docs, config (athena.toml, defaults.toml), ci (.github/) or code (everything else). It refuses a change reading over 3 groups, which means only a reading that spans all four groups, or over 30 deliverables as a backstop. A directory deliverable takes the group of its first path component and the root `.` counts as every group. Study readings and readings with a question are skipped. The error names the bound crossed and the groups found, and says to split the job by surface and dependency and to name the rest in `out_of_scope`. Added `job_size_*` unit tests, six `job-size-*` corpus cases with four new input-form tags, a declared-share test, and a CHANGELOG item. No prompt, config or workflow file changed.

checks_run.note: 1247 lib tests passed, 1 ignored; the other athena-core test binaries passed, except the refusal corpus, which failed once on an accepting case. I fixed the case and reran it.
exit 0; includes athena-cli mirrors and drain tests
17 of 17 passed, so no banned word in tracked files

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs has `pub fn check_job_size(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>` and one `step!(check_job_size(reading));` line in `refusing_check`. Its doc comment names the root cause (nothing before dispatch measured whether a request fits one producer run) and cites jobs 20261025-183644-t67q and 20261017-205554-zaj2.
criteria_check.evidence: Read checks.rs: the function has that signature, `step!(check_job_size(reading));` sits second in `refusing_check`, and the doc comment has the root-cause sentence and both job ids. `cargo test -p athena-core job_size` passed `job_size_has_one_step_line` (exactly one trimmed step line plus the signature) and `job_size_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause` (needles in the collapsed doc comment and the CHANGELOG item).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A new test builds a change reading shaped like job 20261025-183644-t67q (docs, athena.toml, CI workflow, two crates files, xtask, tests, CHANGELOG) and one shaped like 20261017-205554-zaj2 (12 deliverables). `check_job_size` refuses both, and the error says to split the job by surface and dependency. The test fails when the `step!` line is removed.
criteria_check.evidence: `job_size_refuses_the_two_failed_job_shapes` builds both shapes (T67Q_SHAPE: 8 paths plus CHANGELOG.md; ZAJ2_SHAPE: 12 paths plus CHANGELOG.md). It asserts `gate_refuser == Some("check_job_size")` via `refusing_check`, and that the error contains 'too large for one producer run', '4 groups, bound 3', 'split the job by surface and dependency' and 'out_of_scope'. `cargo test -p athena-core` passed (1247 lib tests ok). Without the step line `gate_refuser` could not return Some("check_job_size"), so the assertion fails. I did not run the removal.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. Tests show the bound is general: a focused reading with a few deliverables in one or two surfaces passes. A reading with many deliverables in one crate is refused on count alone, and a study reading and a reading with a question are not refused.
criteria_check.evidence: `job_size_bound_is_general`: 31 files in one crate are refused ('31 deliverables, bound 30'), 30 pass, and CHANGELOG.md is not counted. Four files in four groups are refused, four three-group sets pass, and directory, root and `./` forms are covered. Study, question and no-capability readings are not refused. `job_size_accepts_focused_shapes` has 1 to 3 group readings and a 9-file one-crate reading passing the whole gate. `job_size_refuses_a_backstop_shape_across_crates` refuses 31 paths over several crates. All passed in `cargo test -p athena-core`.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. The refusal corpus (crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs) has a case in which check_job_size is the refusing check, so the corpus test that every `step!` has a refusing case still passes. The existing gate-order tests still pass.
criteria_check.evidence: Added `job_size_cases()` (4 `Expected::Refuse("check_job_size")`, 2 `Expected::Accept`), wired into `cases()`, and 4 tags added to INPUT_FORMS (52 to 56). `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` passed 24 of 24 after I fixed one accepting case that tripped check_environment_reach. The lib tests, including the gate-order tests, passed 1247 of 1247.

criteria_check.criterion: The check refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 6% of newly refused readings, an estimate and not a measurement. CHANGELOG.md has an entry that names the root cause and the new bound.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment and the new item at the end of CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] / Changed carry 'the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 6% of newly refused readings, an estimate and not a measurement'. The item names the root cause, `reading::check_job_size`, the 3-group rule and the 30-deliverable backstop. `job_size_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause` pins the needles. The corpus test `job_size_refusal_is_declared_intended` parses the sentence with `replay_declaration` to `share == Some(6)`. Both passed.

mistakes: My first 3-group accepting corpus case and the stored-reading test used a CI workflow deliverable. check_environment_reach refused both, so the tests failed once. I replaced the workflow with docs.
I started the workspace test in the background and then tried to run it in the foreground. The second run could not get a build slot, which cost a few retries but changed no files.
learnings: `pub use checks::*` in reading.rs exports `check_job_size` to the in-crate tests; private items such as `JobGroup` stay private.

A corpus accepting case with a .github/workflows deliverable is refused by check_environment_reach unless it has an `Environment:` assumption, so the 3-group accepting case uses config, docs and code.
The producer role cannot use grep, head, tail, sleep or heredocs in Bash. Use the Read, Grep and Glob tools, and the Edit tool for file edits.
The build-slot lock makes a second cargo run wait up to 300 s and exit 75 while another run holds it.
